notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: One Switch instance must operate several projects concurrently; switching one project must not stop the others.

notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: Managed development servers have resource priority. Worktree Switcher must be optimized and effectively unnoticeable in idle use; persistence may begin with a file behind a replaceable service layer.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Architecture selected: one lightweight Node controller serves a statically exported Next.js UI and manages processes; versioned JSON is accessed through a ProjectStore adapter; distribution uses the worktree-switcher npm package and foreground CLI.

notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: Decision state: proposed. Discuss visible reservations that pin a server to a worktree and an MCP interface through which an LLM can inspect runtime placement, acquire a reservation, and release it.

notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: Use SQLite from the MVP instead of JSON persistence now that reservations, MCP clients, and audit history require atomic state changes. Keep persistence behind the service boundary.

notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: Use shadcn/ui for the dashboard GUI.

notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: Approved: reservations are MVP scope; controller shutdown stops its owned managed processes; dirty worktrees remain runnable with a visible warning.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Functional prototype implemented: static Next.js/shadcn dashboard, loopback Node controller, SQLite StateStore with transactional audit records and exclusive human reservations, Git porcelain discovery, per-project lifecycle serialization, readiness checks, bounded logs, SSE updates, strict mutation token/origin checks, and owned process-tree shutdown. Automated checks cover Git parsing, reservation exclusion/ownership, owned start-stop, and refusal to kill an unrelated port owner. The backlog remains open: configurable command presets, agent leases/MCP, full CLI, three-project switching validation, browser visual QA, and release resource acceptance are not complete. Measured controller RSS was about 67 MiB before and 68 MiB after a dashboard refresh on Node 24; a bare Node HTTP process on this host measured about 60 MiB, so the 50 MiB RSS target requires revisiting the runtime or metric.

notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: Make the controller reachable from the LAN and add a local firewall exception if required.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: LAN access implemented with a secure boundary: default bind is 0.0.0.0, --host 127.0.0.1 remains available, startup prints a high-entropy pairing URL for the detected LAN address, all API reads/mutations and SSE require the token, and browser mutations require same-host Origin. UFW is active on the reference host, but its rules and changes require interactive sudo unavailable to the agent; the documented rule is restricted to 192.168.1.0/24 and TCP port 47831.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Node launch-command resolution now detects pnpm, npm, yarn, or bun and selects port passing by framework instead of appending a fixed pnpm argument sequence. Next.js and unknown Node servers receive PORT; Vite, Astro, Nuxt, and Angular receive --port through package-manager-specific forwarding. A schema migration replaces the prototype's invalid pnpm dev -- --port command, and registration rejects a missing dev script early. Custom presets for non-Node and unusual frameworks remain open scope.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Per-project Next.js development TLS settings support HTTP, a certificate generated by next dev --experimental-https, or local custom key/certificate/optional CA paths. Settings can change only while the managed process is stopped. Certificate selection is bounded by the controller's file-browser root, and private-key content is never uploaded through the HTTP control plane. This feature secures the managed Next.js server, not the Worktree Switcher dashboard.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: The dashboard now supports Polish and English through a typed local translation layer. A visible PL/EN control persists the user's preference, API and file-browser requests send Accept-Language for localized controller errors, and CLI output follows the operating-system locale.

notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: The dashboard defaults to English regardless of browser locale. Only a saved manual preference selects Polish automatically.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Local MCP integration is implemented as a lazily loaded Streamable HTTP endpoint on a dedicated 127.0.0.1 listener. It uses a persistent owner-only bearer token, exposes project/status/worktree resources and narrow list/status/claim/renew/release tools, and keeps raw lease secrets inside the MCP session. Agent claims are idempotent, owner-authorized, automatically renewed, capped at eight hours, audited, and retained with an explicit error if the claimed server fails to start. Arbitrary commands, arbitrary paths, remote access, and force release are not exposed to MCP. The authenticated dashboard shows listener availability, active session count, endpoint, transport, and access controls without exposing tokens or session identifiers.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: The distribution includes a validated worktree-switcher Agent Skill and packages it under skills/worktree-switcher. The skill teaches agents to inspect placement before acting, acquire an idempotent claim for server work, avoid duplicate dev processes, honor competing reservations, verify startup, and release the claim without exposing credentials. README installation keeps MCP credentials in the client's private configuration and reduces per-repository AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md guidance to a short skill invocation.

notes.author: agent:claude
notes.text: Independent readiness review recorded in NOTE-20260829-readiness-assessment. Tests and typecheck pass, the implementation matches the brief, and the reservation and MCP layer is the capability with no cheap substitute; server switching alone is replaceable by a terminal per worktree. Three gaps were spun off so this item stays focused on the switch flow: CLI project management (FEAT-20260829-cli-project-management), license and first release (FEAT-20260829-license-and-package-release), and the unreachable idle memory target in this item's release validation (RWK-20260829-idle-memory-budget). Until that rework lands, treat the 50 MiB entry in validation as superseded.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Owner prioritizes personal utility, time/token efficiency, and a reusable public experiment. Core implementation exists; this record now owns remaining integrated evidence only. Broad market validation and a runtime rewrite are not prerequisites.

problem: Multi-project switching, the static dashboard, SQLite, reservations, and MCP are implemented. Their integrated failure and resource behavior still needs bounded acceptance evidence, and the assessment found process cleanup and refresh amplification defects.

risk.rollback: Disable process mutation and retain read-only worktree discovery if lifecycle management cannot reliably isolate projects and terminate complete child process trees.

scope: After the linked process and refresh fixes, exercise independent switching, stable ports, reservations, failure isolation, and accurate status with multiple fixture repositories.
Keep the current single-controller architecture and one runtime slot per project. Treat custom launch configuration, test jobs, and distribution through their own items.
Check the owner's normal workflow and one portable fixture workflow. Public adoption targets are not a completion requirement.
title: Complete integrated verification of independent project switching
validation: Switch three isolated fixture projects between worktrees and verify only the selected runtime restarts, ports stay stable, and reservations remain authoritative.
Verify failures, stale worktrees, concurrent requests, and unknown port owners produce truthful status without affecting another project.
Use the measurement procedure from RWK-20260829-idle-memory-budget. The historical 50 MiB absolute threshold is superseded; record runtime baseline, controller overhead, idle CPU, and bounded growth.
Verify affected dashboard controls, keyboard focus, non-color state labels, and persistent dirty-worktree warnings in one focused browser pass.
Verify shutdown and switch remove complete owned process groups using the linked cleanup fix.
value: A developer can move an entire local stack between branches from one dashboard without repeatedly navigating directories or disturbing unrelated services.
